correctness.rationale: Fourier characters provide exactly four doubled nonconstant eigenvalues of every powered resistance distance matrix. The identity for the squared-resistance Gram gap and an explicit three-variable rational inequality prove a strictly positive and sharp floor for all connected real conductances. A one-variable strictly decreasing exponent equation proves the full negative-type interval and equality-space multiplicity. Exact rational 9-by-9 Laplacian inversion on 16 profiles independently reproduces resistances and eigenvalue identities, but is not used to justify universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The network is the smallest noncyclic odd-order abelian Cayley graph, and every connected symmetric translation-invariant conductance assignment is captured by the four direction weights. The result gives a full 4-parameter classification rather than one arbitrary slice: robust Euclidean resistance, the optimal spectral coercivity over the entire family, exact all-p generalized-roundness roots or infinity, and a geometrically meaningful endpoint dimension transition. The unweighted Cartesian 3-by-3 torus receives an exact logarithmic exponent.
